correctness.rationale: Independent enumeration from the five XOR generators gives graph parameters (16,5,0,2), 680 connected four-sets, 192 five-faces and no six-face. The full two-skeleton is forced by the dual definition. On five vertices all deletions connected implies minimum degree at least two; either a triangle-free graph of that order with this property is a pentagon or it is K_{2,3}, which violates the common-neighbor bound. On six vertices the deletion of each other vertex would have to leave any fixed vertex with degree two, impossible. The independent oriented boundary check at /workspace/branches/ec6a89e4-f187-4091-af39-c4a13731b536/independent_clebsch_boundary_check.py (matching _output.txt in the same directory) constructed boundaries rather than reading frozen matrices. It found 455 unit pivots in the 455-by-680 matrix in the full two-skeleton's 2-cycle basis, and 191 unit pivots with zero residual in the 680-by-192 matrix, also verifying the composition vanishes. Thus H_2 vanishes and the fourth-boundary image is primitive in the third cycles. The simply connected third skeleton is then 2-connected by Hurewicz and equivalent by Whitehead to a wedge of 225 three-spheres. In that wedge the attaching classes are exactly their H_3 classes; the homotopy cofiber is preserved by unimodular equivalences on the domain and target sphere wedges. Cancelling the 191 unit pairs leaves S^4 and 34 copies of S^3. With fixed 16-vertex ground set duality sends degrees 4,3 to 9,10. The 1140 equal-size facets give dimension 11, and the two nonzero lower homology groups persist over every field, ruling out both Cohen–Macaulayness and pure shellability. No original-complex wedge type is needed or asserted. Inspected the frozen checker and recorded output as evidence; the independent checker did not execute them.
